headers:
Topdressing and infield mix are stated
in the SOW as "as needed". To be
apples to apples for all responses,
please specify the exact quantity in
cubic yards of all infield mix and
topdress sand to be included in pricing
per site.

DCSD is not establishing a guaranteed quantity of
topdressing or infield mix for each site. Routine quantities
necessary to meet the required performance standards shall
be included in the Contractor's routine pricing. Work
constituting major turf restoration, topsoil placement, field
renovation, or other work outside routine maintenance will
require written authorization under the Optional Services
provisions.

Refer to answers no. 1 and 12.

Synthetic fields - Please clarify what
repairs are included in the base scope
and what repairs are excluded

Routine artificial-turf maintenance includes grooming, infill
redistribution, debris removal, cleaning, magnet sweeping,
seam and edge inspection, drainage observation, and high-
use-area inspection. Specialized repairs to damaged artificial
turf are excluded from routine maintenance and shall be
separately authorized as Optional Services. Running-track
repairs are likewise Optional Services.

headers:
On the excel Spreadsheet the unit of
measure for some of the optional
services states LS. I looked up this
measurement and came up with the
below definition. Is this correct that you
want to use for these additional
services? What unit of measurement is
LS? AI Overview In measurement and
business documents, "LS" most
commonly stands for Lump Sum,
acting as a single, all-inclusive unit of
measure for a project task or item
rather than individual counts or
measurements.

Yes. “LS” means Lump Sum: one all-inclusive price for the
complete authorized Optional Service described in the
applicable work authorization, including all labor, supervision,
equipment, materials, transportation, mobilization, overhead,
profit, disposal and incidentals unless DCSD expressly states
otherwise.
sample:

Identifies additional services. Is it

Vendors should provide the requested Optional Services unit
pricing. Optional Services are not guaranteed work and will
only be performed when specifically authorized in writing by
DCSD. Submission of unit pricing does not guarantee that
DCSD will purchase any quantity of an Optional Service.

Will the schools be divided into
“zones,” as briefly mentioned during
the site visit?

DCSD reserves the right to award one or more Geographic
Service Areas and to modify assignments during the Contract
Term as operational needs require.

headers:
Can you clarify what needs to be
included in the line item pricing for
"erosion control measures?"

“Erosion Control Measures - LS” means the complete cost of
District-authorized erosion-control work defined in a specific
work authorization. The lump-sum price shall include all labor,
materials, equipment, installation, stabilization,
removal/disposal, and incidentals required to complete the
authorized work. Scope and quantity will be defined by DCSD
before authorization.
sample:
5.2 On page 25 - Event areas,
associated, spectator - please clarify
these areas.

“Athletic Event Areas,” “Associated Grounds,” and “Spectator
Buffer Areas” mean areas directly associated with and
necessary for operation of the designated athletic facility, as
identified by DCSD's site map or work assignment. They do
not include general campus landscaping or unrelated grounds
outside the designated athletic-maintenance boundary.

Please provide a field-by-field
inventory confirming which of the 11
pricing categories actually apply at
each of the 44 facilities (not every site
has
football/baseball/softball/track/synthetic
turf) — Appendix A gives acreage but
not field type counts per site.

Please see site maps included in addendum no. 2. Please
refer to the Cost Proposal Form (Attachment A-1) to identify
which service categories apply to each facility. Vendors shall
not assume that all routine-service categories apply to every
location. Only applicable categories should be priced for each
facility. Existing conditions and final assignments will be
verified during the baseline site assessment.

Please confirm expected turf height on
fields.

Natural turf shall be maintained at an appropriate playing
height for the turf species, season, field use, and applicable
scholastic athletic standards. The Contractor shall maintain a
uniform, healthy and safe playing surface consistent with
SFMA best management practices and University of Georgia
Turfgrass guidance. DCSD is not establishing one universal
mowing height for every natural-turf field.
